Note::is_ascii¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::is_ascii() const

Test Whether Every Byte In A Cell Is ASCII¶

is_ascii() reports, for each cell, whether every byte is in the range 0x00–0x7F. Use it to check that a field will survive an ASCII-only channel unchanged, to route non-ASCII rows to a normalization step, or to confirm that a byte-level operation (the ASCII case predicates, the ASCII tokenizers) will behave as intended on that cell.

Unlike the character-class predicates, is_ascii() on an empty cell is 1 — vacuously, every byte (none) is ASCII.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"plain", "", "café", "日本語", "a\tb"});
const auto mask = n.is_ascii();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0, 0, 1]

"café" and "日本語" have bytes >= 0x80; "a\tb" is fine (tab is 0x09).

See Also¶

  • Note::is_utf8_valid: a weaker check — well-formed UTF-8, ASCII or not.

  • pluss::coden::Note::to_ascii / transliterate_ascii: coerce a cell to ASCII.

  • Note::lengths_bytes vs Note::lengths_chars: they agree exactly when is_ascii() is 1.
